description.narrative:
The Ministry of Manpower issued a study on the impact of energy transition on jobs that will be a base for a Manpower Roadmap for energy transition in Indonesia. The Government of Indonesia formed a secretariat for the JET Partnership, as a result of their commitment to net zero emissions which was announced in the G20 meeting in 2022. The JETP aims to produce the Comprehensive Investment and Policy Plan (CIPP) of the Government of Indonesia, which includes measures for Just Transition. The National Development Planning Agency (Bappenas) together with the ILO and Partnership for Green Economy conducted an assessment of policy readiness for just transition which is used for policymakers. A Green Jobs Forum: Transitioning to a Green and Blue Economy was organized in North Sulawesi, Indonesia, which discussed various issues of employment in relation to sustainable tourism and biodiversity. The study is commissioned by the Ministry of Manpower to be conducted by the ILO. The ILO was invited to be a part of the JETP working group on Just Transition of the Government of Indonesia and provided input to the CIPP.
The ILO conducted the study for Bappenas and results were disseminated.
The ILO organized this forum for policymakers and other stakeholders in ASEAN in collaboration with the UN, with funding support from the Government of Japan.

description.narrative:
‘Sinar Usaha Budo’ Bumdes - a village-owned enterprise, was formed to facilitate the growth of eco-tourism and micro-enterprises in the Budo village.
Currently, the Bumdes Budo has reported income amounting to IDR 1,343,880,003 (USD 92,681.38) from September 2021 to April 2023, generated from various micro business activities like mangrove trail ticketing, parking area, local food and beverages produced, and homestay, and also assets of infrastructure and facilities from CSR Central Bank, Pelindo, PLN Peduli) equivalent to IDR 1,266,000,000 (USD 87,310.34).
For this progress, the Ministry of Tourism and Creative Economy (MoTCE) has promoted Budo Tourism Village as a pilot of a sister villages programme among four countries in ASEAN, called BIMP-EAGA (Brunei Darussalam, Indonesia, Malaysia, and the Philippines East Asia Growth Area) knowledge sharing platform, and to connect among the villages for promoting sustainable tourism development Supported by the Government of UK, Budo is one of the beneficiaries among 3 other villages (Tiwoho, Marinsow, and Pulisan) of the North Minahasa District of the North Sulawesi Province in developing eco-tourism in the coastal area. The village has successfully developed a new tourist destination that was nominated for the top 50 village tourism award in 2022 and the winner of the digital creative category.
With funding support from the United Kingdom, the Bumdes Sinar Jaya was established in September 2021 and started to manage micro businesses in the Budo village. The Bumdes was initially supported by the village funds in the form of infrastructure and facilities of the mangrove trail as a tourist spot to attract visitors from surrounding Manado to see sunset of Bunaken island.
In addition, the tourism development of Budo village is a pilot case of the development of coastal tourism in which the local community optimized the maritime sector through sustainable economic tourism activities for the blue economy agenda.
